content.text:

content.text: Yeah, and then I asked Amar about your pricing, and then she mentioned that it was just a flat rate per project. Is that the same for Agent Fabric as well, or how does the pricing work?

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: Okay. Generally, it's not per project. For a regular Mulesoft implementation, bonus it's $3,500 per floor and for IP, it is $3,000 per document type. Okay, let me pull up your... Okay, let me know if you can see my screen.

content.speaker: bsergienko@salesforce.com
content.text: Yeah. I can see it now.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text:
I'm just getting to the slides side of that. So if you see here, the pricing is pretty straight in terms of Mulesoft if it's MULE for flow. Every floor, we charged at $1,500 bucks. If from Salesforce to Nextt Suite Opportunity Closure going to create a sales order is $1,500 bucks.
If an invoice is created in NetSuite, we want that info to come back to Salesforce. That is another flow. That is another $1,500 bucks. Similarly, if the same use cases go for platform, it is $3,500 per floor and IDP any top type is $3,000. That means if it's, let's assume, there is a purchase order, that would be $3,000.
If it's an invoice, that would be $3,000. These are for simple and medium complexity. If the variance is huge, the number of pages is huge, then the price would change. So if the use case says that they will receive a purchase order via email, we need to pick it up and call IDP extract the info and put it into Salesforce. Then that would be $6,500.
But if they get it via email, they get it via SharePoint, they get it via Slack. Then it would be three flows. That would be $10,500 plus $3,000 is $13,500. So that is how the whole pricing works. But again, it is very competitive, and we have implemented close to the last two months. We have done almost at least five IDP projects and overall close to 20 IDP projects.
So we are pretty comfortable with IDP and the platform has been better. But Wave and Informatica... If it's a simple, straightforward use case, the data lives inside Salesforce. They want to have a job that runs and cleans up two objects.
That is accounts and contacts, for example. Then that is $4,000, but if it is accounts, objects, and opportunities, then the price would increase up to $7,000 to $9,000. So only two objects, it's $4,000. The more and more objects that have to be cleaned, then the price keeps increasing.

content.text: The two...

Then we extract them and insert them into Salesforce as well. Coming to the agent fabric part, let me share my screen. Okay. Just pulling up the slide. Sorry for that.
Okay, so our gigantic part of it is $25,000. If you can see my screen, this is the slide that we are doing. Okay, so if you see...

content.text: Yeah. I can see. Its...

content.text:

So it's $25K for Agent Fabric.

content.speaker: bsergienko@salesforce.com
content.text: Makes sense.

content.speaker: kailash chanda
content.text: So here is the fixed scope. Right? So that's why she called out that for Agent Fabric, it is a fixed scope. 3 MC servers and three agents...
